scope: All nineteen wrong report-supplied cases in the completed frozen thirty-question sample.
reviewer: AI-assisted execution review, not independent human annotation or blinded adjudication.
method: Read saved raw predictions, reference answers/derivations, full tables and relevant/cited paragraphs locally. Public records contain only UID/category/metadata, never benchmark question, answer or quoted report text. No prediction, scoring rule, label or published metric changed.
causal_limit: Primary labels describe observed failure modes, not inaccessible internal model reasoning. Citations show claimed support, not necessarily the operands the model actually used. Matching a reference derivation does not resolve ambiguous wording.

primary_categories.multi_answer_serialization: Requested reference components appear in one joined string rather than separate spans.
primary_categories.numeric_result_mismatch: A numeric output differs from the reference calculation; actual internal operands/operation are not assumed.
primary_categories.unit_only_mismatch: The answer value component matches the reference but its scale/dimension does not.
primary_categories.operator_or_denominator_convention: The response and reference use different quantity, rate-change or denominator conventions.
primary_categories.cited_operand_mapping_mismatch: A claimed supporting input is a derived or otherwise inappropriate table column.
primary_categories.period_comparison_mismatch: The returned period does not match the requested comparison.
primary_categories.reference_span_boundary: The response is a shorter supported span than the stored reference; independent adjudication is needed.

items.note: The reference components are present in the prediction string. Claimed support points to a blank header band rather than the year headers.
The cited cell pair supplies the requested inputs, but its mean does not match the prediction. The scale also differs; actual internal calculation is unknown.
Both reference values and their units are present, but emitted as a single sentence-like string rather than two spans.
The cited inputs support the reference percentage calculation, not the emitted result. A simple reversed-period formula does not explain the prediction.
The dimensionless count value matches the reference, but the prediction attaches a monetary scale.

The reference uses a rate-point difference while the output resembles a signed relative change. The magnitude wording and operator convention need review; the cited periods also differ from the requested pair.
The prediction differs from recomputed percentage change beyond the reference rounding precision; the cited input cells match the requested pair.
The single value component matches the reference but is labelled as a percentage instead of a dimensionless count.
The shorter response is supported by its source quote but omits the stored reference prefix. Retain the native error; do not silently relabel it.
The requested pair is present with the reference scale, but joined into one string instead of separate spans.
The output differs from the fixed reference calculation. One cited period is outside the requested pair, so the actual operands remain uncertain.
The prediction aligns with an alternate denominator, while the question does not clearly name a base. Cited cells target a component row rather than the requested aggregate.
The selected year conflicts with the source comparison and a dimensionful unit is attached to the year. No supporting citation was supplied.
All requested reference names are present but serialized as one span. Saved native F1 is full while exact match is zero; that distinction is preserved.
A cited input is an already-computed variance column rather than the second requested period. The output value and unit also disagree with the reference; actual internal operands are unknown.
The prediction copies a displayed relative variance, while the reference uses an amount difference. The quantity convention warrants independent review rather than an automatic factual-error claim.
The response is a relative rate while the reference is an amount difference. One cited coordinate is a label, not a numeric operand; the emitted value is not explained by the reference calculation.
The output magnitude is inconsistent with the mean of the correctly cited percentage cells. Internal decimal handling is not observed.
The output differs from the reference mean and cites an adjacent metric row. Whether the error arose in reading or arithmetic cannot be determined from citations alone.

recommendations_not_implemented: First fix the generic multi-answer contract on invented development fixtures: allow separate ordered spans instead of forcing a scalar. Do not repair or regrade these four exposed cases.
Add typed operands naming row, period and unit, then deterministic arithmetic validation; a calculator without correct operand mapping is insufficient.
Validate answer dimension separately from table units, especially counts, years, amount changes, relative changes and rate-point changes.
Treat location/quote checks as syntax/support-location checks, not semantic grounding; review cited target alignment.
Independently adjudicate span/operator ambiguities before using these observations as new training labels. Preserve original gold and metrics.
Any later model validation uses a newly frozen fresh sample excluding all130 already exposed question IDs; no model training or rerun is authorized here.
non_claims: No corrected accuracy, recovered-correct count, new prediction score, training label set, formal H1 or financial result.

provenance.raw_text_location: Ignored data/reader_error_audit only; not a public artifact.

interpretation: Counts overlap across flags. These observations do not revise11/30EM, demonstrate a fix, identify every internal cause, or establish that ambiguous references are wrong. Seven wrong cases have reference-scale mismatches; the eighth full-sample scale miss is outside this19-case error set.

validation.reason: Documentation/data-only audit; no production code, predictions or scoring changed. Explicit JSON/scope/count/hash/privacy/link checks performed; prior test results are not presented as rerun.
